questions.question: Which staining reagent is commonly used to increase electron density of lipids and membranes in TEM?
In TEM, what is the role of the objective aperture?

answers.a: To accelerate electrons to higher energy
answers.b: To select central beam for diffraction only
answers.c: To improve image contrast by limiting scattered electrons
answers.d: To cool the sample during imaging

questions.question: What causes "beam damage" in biological samples during TEM?

answers.b: High electron dose causing radiolysis and heating

questions.question: Which embedding resin is commonly used for ultramicrotomy of biological samples?
Which contrast mechanism is most important for imaging unstained biological specimens in TEM under cryo conditions?
Which grid support film is commonly used for TEM biological samples to reduce contamination and provide support?
Which heavy metal stain binds strongly to nucleic acids and proteins in TEM?
In TEM sample preparation, what is the purpose of ultramicrotomy?

answers.b: To cut ultrathin sections (~50-100 nm) for transmission

questions.question: In TEM, contrast due to atomic number differences (Z-contrast) is most prominent in which imaging mode?

answers.b: Dark-field imaging or high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) in STEM

questions.question: Why is glow-discharge treatment applied to TEM grids before sample application?

answers.b: To make the carbon film hydrophilic and improve sample spreading
